items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But I never knew Rex. I never listened to Rex.

ctx.x: Speaking of Rex Stewart, I don’t know whether I would call it a controversy or not, but this is a quote that I got from your responding to someone saying that you got your style from Rex Stewart: “with regard to the so-called half-valve thing, it’s not true that I derive my style from Rex Stewart.”

That’s true. I didn’t. Actually the only time I used the half-valve was when my valves stick or something. I’m too busy trying to make many notes instead of slurring on a note, except that when I did that little funny thing on “What fools you mortals be” on Puck. But I never knew Rex. I never listened to Rex. As a matter of fact, I hadn’t heard too much of the Ellington band before I got – had a chance to be around it, after – of course Rex was gone long since then.
But to achieve those effects, or effects like that, did you use things other than the half-valve?
